questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important for me to choose a university that is/was high ranked and recognized as international university ranking. Furthermore It was important for me that to choose an university that had high level in terms of language, culture and linguistic studies. 
In terms of location, it was important for me to choose a city that had a rich culture life to fulfill that objetive of the Erasmus exchange as a culture travel as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was quite easy to find the relevant information on the Complutense webpage, and/or contacting the international office for philology if the needed information was not to be found on the webpage. Otherwise the information e-mails received told you most of what you needed to know related to deadlines, enrollment, choosing courses, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I received assistance in the enrollment to the programe of students with disabilities to have the tools needed for my dyslexia. 
Furthermore I received assistance to get the Learning Agreement properly signed by the international office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was quite easy to find an apartment through
www.spotahome.com
, but it is important to be early out in terms of finding an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Madrid is a big international city with many exchange student, therefore it is important to be early out to find an apartment or a room with good location and a good price.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1) I had to make the learning agreement and get it signed by both sending and hosting institution. 
2) I had to register myself as a student (and get accepted) in the enrollment page of Complutense. The information and link for this was sent by e-mail. You're not officially accepted at Complutense until this part in completed.
3) I had to make an Complutense e-mail to get access to Campus Virtual. The information for this is also sent to you by e-mail.
4) When the semester started, I had to make an enrollment with my informations and the information of each course chosen, and have it signed physically by the international office of philology.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Most information you need, you can find on the university webpage and/or contacting the international office by e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1) When choose the courses (already in the learning agreement) check the timeslots and weekdays for the courses you would like, and make a schedule to make sure that the courses do not overlap.
2) Look at more courses that the once you've chosen, the first 2 weeks you can change courses. Take advantage of this opportunity to try diferent courses the first week, and be open minded to a change because it's very likely that someone of the courses you've chosen is not what you expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of teaching and the content of the course/each class is very high with a lot of extra information than needed. 
In terms of spanish language and literature, the level in the classroom is very high both regarding to the texts you have to read, activities in the classroom and the assignments you have to make.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching in the classroom (in most classes) is similar to that what I experienced at UCPH.
But, there is not room for question in the same way. Therefore, what you don't feel that you've learned properly, it is your responsibility to learn by your own or ask for a tutor meeting with your profesor. 
Furthermore, each course as fever ECTS which means that you have a lot more courses and more classes that all have a very high demand in assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Retórica y crítica literaria
Sociolingüística española
Lingüística y estudios culturales
Enseñanza de español como lengua extranjera 
El cuento hispanoamericano

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Lingüística y estudios culturales. 
The professor Viviane Martins has a different way of teaching than the majority of the professors, that both make the classroom comfortable for the students, but also by incorporating many assignments and presentations according to each subject. This also means that assignment demand is very high, be aware of this.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since it is an intense and stressfull semester, in my case, my health was weaker than expected and I got frequently sick. Therefore the price for medicine was not something i encounter.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The local transport is cheaper than expected. When you're less than 25, you can get a public transport card (for metro, trains and buses) for 8€ a month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of different type of "fitness"-classes such as: Pilates, yoga, zumba, merengue, swimming etc. 
Sports activities in teams such as: football, rugby, tennis, etc.
Cultural and creative activities such as: theatre, music, etc. 
Social activities was mostly organized by the group ESN UCM.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to to buy the sports-card from UCM (90€ for the whole semester), this gives you access to the university gym, and any sports class that you would like. Personally I took a lot of pilates classes. Highly recormended as they are in the middle of the day, so it is a nice break and renewing energy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Every sunday (and everyday during summer) there is social salsa and bachata dancing in front of the Ermita curch in the center of the city. Really fun and local experience. 
Furthermore, Madrid has endless cultural opportunities, especially theater, and as a student you often get discount so each play is quite cheap compared to going to the theater in Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since I have already previously lived a year in Spain it was quite easy to easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take initiative, ask for their contact and talk with them in the classroom.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the public system in terms of the doctor and getting medicine is not as effective as I was used to, so you have to both patient and bushy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The extremely rich culture life of Madrid and the vibrant life on the streets.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be aware of a high demand of assignments in each course that are both time consuming and challenging on an academic level. Make an overview of the assignments you have to make in each course and start early in the semester, because there will not be time to do them all in the end of the semester. 
2) Be aware of each professor has their individual way of using Campus Virtual, and for most courses there is not much information online. Furthermore, there is not an overview of the semester and its contents in terms of a semesterplan. Therefore it is also:
3) Extremely important to take a lot of notes in class, since most of the professor doesn't upload their powerpoint after the classes or does not use a powerpoint. In other words, your output of the class is mostly based on your notes. Therefore attendance in the classes is also very important.
4) Ask! Don't be to shy to ask fellow student, the international office, take advantage of the opportunity of getting individual tutoring by your professor.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. Most of the information you need, you'll get throughout the semester. But if your in doubt, don't hold back from asking.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My spanish has improved significantly both oral, written and reading.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The semester is short (4 months including exams), and very intens with a high demand of assignments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
